title: Plots and Mary Queen of Scots Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll uncover the Catholic plots against Elizabeth and Mary's execution.

final_note: You learned how Walsingham's spies foiled plot after plot before 1587.

concepts.def: Catholic cousin who fled to England in 1568
1571 plan for Spanish invasion and Mary as Queen
1583 — French invasion plan, foiled by Walsingham
1586 — letters trapped Mary in a treason scheme
Spymaster whose agents broke the plots

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1568 Mary Queen of Scots fled to England after defeat at Langside.

Elizabeth imprisoned her — but Catholics saw Mary as the true Queen. In 1569 the Northern Earls rebelled and in 1570 Pope Pius V excommunicated Elizabeth.

In 1571 Roberto Ridolfi plotted a Spanish invasion and Mary's marriage to the Duke of Norfolk.

Norfolk was executed in 1572. In 1583 Francis Throckmorton's letters to Mary uncovered a French plot. Walsingham's spy network foiled both.

In 1586 Anthony Babington wrote to Mary about a Spanish invasion.

Walsingham intercepted every letter via a beer-barrel post. Mary endorsed regicide in writing — sealing her fate. She was beheaded at Fotheringhay on 8 February 1587.
